_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 5 $8155-$8353: the room buffer builder (slot $8003) - structure, door set, item list, layout and key doors. The generators subtract these.

regions.name: BUILD THE ROOM BUFFER (slot $8003): wait for the decompressor
regions.description: Slot $8003 -> $8155, called by every room loader ($EBC0, $EE80, $EEFD and others). JSR $C045 (-> $D7C3) waits until the tile decompressor is idle: the scene's tiles must be in before a room is drawn. (A harness without NMIs spins here; the checks below start at $8158.) The result is the 16 x 12 buffer at $0740 (192 bytes, one metatile id per 16-pixel cell, row by row) plus the four exit/key bytes $58-$5B and $54.

regions.name: Room buffer: pick the structure, door set and item list
regions.description: JSR $A749 selects the room's STRUCTURE ($18/$19), DOOR SET ($14/$15) and ITEM LIST ($16/$17): for an ordinary room entry 2 x $50 (the area) of the three tables, for a special screen the tables indexed by the screen type $51 (see the room-drawing notes).

regions.name: Room buffer: tile the structure's pattern
regions.description: A structure is [list offset][dest][width][height][pattern: width x height ids]. The pattern is copied into the buffer from offset dest and TILED: each row of the pattern repeats across to the end of the 16-cell row, rows are taken in turn, and after `height` rows the pattern starts again, until the buffer is full ($C0). A 1 x 1 structure is a plain floor. $12 is the row's start offset, $1B/$11 the width counter and width, $1A the rows left, $10 the pattern offset. RUN: the real routine built the room buffer for 302 rooms (ordinary rooms and special screens: every map record except the 21 gates and the empty cells) and the buffer equalled the independent model in tools/parse-structs.py in all of them, apart from the key-door cells noted at $82DD.

regions.name: Room buffer: the structure's own items
regions.description: The structure's first byte is an offset to a group of four [length][item] records (or to a zero byte for none); when it is not zero JSR $8379 draws them.

regions.name: Room buffer: the door set's four fixed items
regions.description: $19:$18 := the door set; $8379 draws its first four [length][item]s (walls and decoration that every room of the area has); $14 := the offset reached, where the four per-exit items follow.

regions.name: Room buffer: special screens have no exits
regions.description: $30 bit 5 (a special screen) skips the four exit walls and goes straight to the item list at $8227.

regions.name: Room buffer: read the openings
regions.description: $15 := byte 1 of the room's map record: bits 7, 6, 5, 4 = exits open to the north, west, east, south.

regions.name: Room buffer: north wall
regions.description: The door set's next item is the WALL across the north exit. It is drawn ($A6EB) when the north neighbour's record has bit 7 set in byte 0 (empty cell or special screen) or the room's north opening bit is clear; either way $14 advances past the item. So a wall is drawn across every exit that does not lead to an ordinary room.

regions.name: Room buffer: west wall
regions.description: The same with the west neighbour ($E2) and opening bit 6.

regions.name: Room buffer: east wall
regions.description: The same with the east neighbour ($E6) and opening bit 5.

regions.name: Room buffer: south wall
regions.description: The same with the south neighbour ($E8) and opening bit 4; an open south exit to an ordinary room jumps straight to $8227. At the map's EDGE the neighbour pointer has a high byte of 0 and the code reads ZERO PAGE: 47 rooms; the byte can have bit 7 set (129 and 137 were read), but the outcome is the same either way because an edge room has no opening there (all 47 matched the model).

regions.name: Room buffer: the item list
regions.description: The item list is a $0000-ended run of pointers to bare items [dest][width][height][tiles]; each is drawn with $A6EB (width bit 7 = one tile repeated, height bit 7 = the tiles are behind a pointer, $00 transparent). This is where a room's rocks, doors and decorations come from.

regions.name: Room buffer: the room's own layout pointer
regions.description: Byte 0 bit 4 of the record says a layout pointer is present, else jump to $82DD. The pointer follows the optional fields: Y = 3, +1 if there is a script id ($57), +1 if the kind is not 0 or $60 (a sub-id); $18/$19 := the layout.

regions.name: Layout: the shape and its fill tile
regions.description: A layout is [shape | count << 5][tile] + count x [tile][pos][mask | dir]. $8042 turns the shape number (byte 0 AND $1F) into the shape's address ($16); $10 := the tile; X := $20 (row 2 of the buffer).

regions.name: Layout: paint the shape
regions.description: The shape is 18 bytes of 1 bit per cell, most significant bit first: every set bit stores the tile at the next buffer cell (144 cells = rows 2-10).

regions.name: Layout: how many extra lines?
regions.description: Byte 0 bits 5-7 (rotated down) = the number of extra tile lines; zero goes to $82DD.

regions.name: Layout: paint the extra lines
regions.description: Each line is [tile][start position][mask | dir]: the top two bits of the third byte pick a step from the table at $82D9 (-15, +1, +16, +17: up-right, right, down, down-right) and the low six bits say which of the six cells along that direction receive the tile. Used for the lone rocks, doors and special tiles.

regions.name: Key doors: reset the four exit keys
regions.description: $58-$5B := 8 for N, W, E, S: 'no key needed'.

regions.name: Key doors: the openings and this room's byte 0
regions.description: $15 and $54 := byte 1 of the record (the openings, bits 7-4, and bit 3 = the room has enemies: CORRECTION to the note that bit 3 of $54 was unexplained) and $14 := byte 0.

regions.name: Key doors: north exit
regions.description: If the north opening bit is set and (the neighbour's byte 0 OR this room's byte 0) has bit 7 set, a special screen lies on one side: the exit gets a KEY DOOR. $58 := the neighbour's byte 1 AND 7 (the key number its record names, 0 = no key) and metatile 8 (the door) is written to buffer cell $0777 (row 3, column 7). RUN: every exit whose $58-$5B was not 8 had metatile 8 in its door cell, and those were the only cells that differed from the model: 131 doors in the 302 rooms (1 door in 83 rooms, 2 in 19, 3 in 2, 4 in 1).

regions.name: Key doors: west exit
regions.description: The same for the west exit with opening bit 6: $59 and the door cell $07B2 (row 7, column 2). CORRECTION: the $0777 / $07B2 / $07BD / $07E7 lead in the weapons notes - they are these four door cells.

regions.name: Key doors: east exit
regions.description: $5A and the door cell $07BD (row 7, column 13).

regions.name: Key doors: south exit
regions.description: $5B and the door cell $07E7 (row 10, column 7); RTS. These four cells are the ones the cleared-gate code ($EEB7) opens (8 -> $0C).
